algorithm: autoregressive next-token prediction over discretized (256-bin per-dimension, quantile-based) action tokens, single-step (no action chunking)
arm: WidowX (BridgeData V2), Google-robot mobile manipulator, Franka Emika Panda (Franka-Tabletop, Franka-DROID); all single fixed or mobile-base arms
sim: LIBERO benchmark (simulated Franka) for fine-tuning experiments; engine/version not stated
success_criterion: binary success (1)/failure (0) per rollout, with explicit partial credit (0.5) defined per-task in several tasks
headline_value: 'outperforming closed models such as RT-2-X (55B) by 16.5% in absolute task success rate across 29 tasks' (Abstract); BridgeData V2: OpenVLA 70.6+/-3.2% vs RT-2-X 50.6+/-3.5% (Table 4, 170 rollouts); Google robot: OpenVLA 85.0+/-4.6% vs RT-2-X 78.3+/-5.4% (Table 6, 60 rollouts)
note_gaps: Function/class bodies for the core tokenizer and model files (action_tokenizer.py, openvla.py) are not present in code/md (only signatures), so the exact bin-decoding arithmetic could not be independently verified against the paper's quantile description.
backbone: Prismatic-7B VLM (600M-parameter visual encoder [SigLIP + DinoV2, concatenated channel-wise] + small 2-layer MLP projector + 7B-parameter Llama 2 language backbone)
action_head: none -- autoregressive next-token prediction over discretized action tokens (256 bins per dimension, overwriting the 256 least-used tokens in the Llama tokenizer vocabulary)
pretrain_data: Open X-Embodiment, 970k trajectories (vs. 350k used by RT-2-X)
dexterous_evidence: "We evaluate OpenVLA's performance 'out-of-the-box' on two robot embodiments: the WidowX robot from the BridgeData V2 evaluations ... and the mobile manipulation robot from the RT-1 and RT-2 evaluations ('Google robot')" (§5.1), together with "We test OpenVLA in two setups: Franka-Tabletop... and Franka-DROID" (§5.2) -- all parallel-jaw gripper platforms, with the gripper encoded as a single scalar 'Grip' action dimension.
